# Eliza Andrews

- **Age:** 57  <sub>[v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P29](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0029)</sub>

## Personality

Eliza Andrews is known for her deeply pessimistic outlook, often serving as a benchmark for gloomy perspectives. Despite her negative disposition, she is very fond of her husband.

_Sources: [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P60](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0060), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P24](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0024), [v2 XVII A Chapter of Accidents P64](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0064), [v2 XXII Odds and Ends P12](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0012)_

## History

Eliza Andrews lived in a small brown house situated in a sunny corner of Mark Andrew's beech woods. While canvassing for the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers) to raise money for the hall, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) visited her, but Eliza met them with a grim refusal.

_Sources: [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P12](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0012), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P14](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0014), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P16](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0016), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P30](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0030), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P36](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0036)_

## Quotes

> "I don’t see the necessity. We didn’t gad about to halls and places when we were young, Catherine Andrews. This world is getting worse every day."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P18](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0018)

> "Doctors always talk like that just to keep people cheered up. I wouldn’t have much hope if I was her. It’s best to be prepared for the worst."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P27](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0027)

> “You think!” Miss Eliza’s voice expressed the utmost contempt. “It doesn’t signify what you think, Catherine Andrews. Facts is facts.”
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P20](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0020)

> "There isn’t any bright side."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P22](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0022)
